title: Derived Boolean coatom excision with an explicit quotient representative
statement: Let $E$ be a finite set with $|E|\geq2$, let $a\in E$, and put $v=E\setminus\{a\}$. For any finite set $F$, let $P_F=\{S\subseteq F:\varnothing\ne S\ne F\}$ ordered by inclusion and let $B_F=C(P_F;\mathbf Q)$ be the augmented strict-chain complex of [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains]. Let $D=P_E\setminus\{v\}$ with its induced order. The assignment $S\mapsto S\cup\{a\}$ is a monotone endomorphism of $D$, pointwise above both its identity and its constant map at $\{a\}$, and $C(D;\mathbf Q)$ is acyclic in all integer degrees. The chain-basis inclusion $C(D;\mathbf Q)\hookrightarrow B_E$ is the identity in degree $-1$; let $V$ be its degreewise quotient complex. Define the suspension by $(\Sigma B_v)_n=(B_v)_{n-1}$ and $d^{\Sigma}_n=-d^{B_v}_{n-1}$. For $n\geq0$, the formula $\theta_n([S_0<\cdots<S_{n-1}<v]\bmod C_n(D;\mathbf Q))=(-1)^n[S_0<\cdots<S_{n-1}]$, with $[v]$ sent to $[\varnothing]$ when $n=0$, defines a chain isomorphism $\theta:V\cong\Sigma B_v$; in negative degrees it is the unique map between zero spaces. Write $\check K^q=K_{-q}$ for reversal from chain to cochain grading and $Q$ for localization into $D(\mathbf Q\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If $p:B_E\to V$ is the quotient, then $Q(\check\theta\circ\check p):Q(\check B_E)\longrightarrow Q(\check B_v)[1]$ is an isomorphism in this derived category.

proof.text: Put $e=\{a\}$ and $u(S)=S\cup\{a\}$. Since $|E|\geq2$, $e$ is nonempty and proper, and $e\ne v$, so $e\in D$. For $S\in D$, $u(S)$ is nonempty and contains $a$, hence is not $v$. If $u(S)=E$, then $v\subseteq S$; as $E\setminus v=\{a\}$, this forces $S=v$ or $S=E$, both excluded. Thus $u$ maps $D$ to $D$. Inclusion is preserved by union, and $S\subseteq u(S)$ and $e\subseteq u(S)$ prove $\operatorname{id}_D\leq u$ and $c_e\leq u$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-poset-augmented-chain-prism] with $R=\mathbf Q$ and $P=Q=D$ to both comparisons from step 1. For $n\geq0$ set $t_n=h_n(c_e,u)-h_n(\operatorname{id}_D,u)$, and put $t_{-1}[\varnothing]=[e]$, with $t_n=0$ below $-1$. The difference of the prism identities is $d t+t d=\operatorname{id}-(c_e)_*$ before the degree $-1$ correction. In degrees $n\geq1$ the constant map kills every strict chain (its image repeats a vertex), and the correction has no component there. In degree zero, $(c_e)_*$ sends every vertex to $[e]$; the added term $t_{-1}d$ sends every vertex to $[e]$ as well, so $d t_0+t_{-1}d=\operatorname{id}$. In degree $-1$, $d t_{-1}[\varnothing]=d[e]=[\varnothing]$. Below $-1$ all spaces vanish. Hence $d t+t d=\operatorname{id}$ in every degree. If $z$ is a cycle, $z=d(tz)$, so the kernel modulo image definition in [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] gives $H_n(C(D;\mathbf Q))=0$ for all $n\in\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains], the strict chains avoiding $v$ form a subset of the chain basis of $B_E$, closed under deletion. Their inclusion therefore commutes with the differential and is injective in every degree. It fixes the empty generator in degree $-1$. In each degree the quotient $V_n$ is free on the complementary basis: chains containing $v$; $V_n=0$ for $n<0$. Since $v$ is maximal in $P_E$, every surviving chain has the unique form $[S_0<\cdots<S_{n-1}<v]$. Its preceding vertices are exactly a strict chain of nonempty proper subsets of $v$. For $n=0$ this preceding chain is empty. Dropping the last vertex is consequently a bijection from the quotient basis to the basis of $(B_v)_{n-1}$.

proof.text: For a surviving basis element $b=[S_0<\cdots<S_{n-1}<v]$ with $n\geq1$, its quotient differential is $d_V b=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(-1)^i[S_0<\cdots<\widehat S_i<\cdots<S_{n-1}<v]$: the face deleting $v$ lies in $C(D;\mathbf Q)$ and vanishes. Write $c=[S_0<\cdots<S_{n-1}]$. Using the deletion differential in [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains], $\theta_{n-1}d_Vb=(-1)^{n-1}d_{B_v}c$, while $d_{\Sigma B_v}\theta_n b=-(-1)^n d_{B_v}c$. These coincide, including $n=1$ where $d_{B_v}[S_0]=[\varnothing]$. In degree zero both differentials out of the source and target are zero, and negative degrees are zero. Thus $\theta$ is a chain map. Its inverse on a degree $n$ basis element is $c\mapsto(-1)^n[c<v]$, with the empty chain sent to $[v]$; the two composites multiply by $(-1)^{2n}=1$. Hence it is the asserted chain isomorphism.

proof.text: The inclusion and quotient give a degreewise short exact sequence $0\to C(D;\mathbf Q)\to B_E\xrightarrow{p}V\to0$ by the basis description in step 3. Reversing the integer indices produces a degreewise short exact sequence of cochain complexes of $\mathbf Q$-modules. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. Step 2 makes the terms on either side of $H^q(\check p)$ zero for every $q$, so exactness gives $H^q(\check p):H^q(\check B_E)\cong H^q(\check V)$. Thus $\check p$ is a quasi-isomorphism in the sense of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: Reversal sends the chain isomorphism of step 4 and its inverse to inverse cochain maps. Moreover $(\check{\Sigma B_v})^q=(B_v)_{-q-1}=(\check B_v)^{q+1}$ and its differential is $-d_{B_v}$, exactly the shift convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; thus $\check{\Sigma B_v}=\check B_v[1]$. The composite $\check\theta\circ\check p$ is a quasi-isomorphism: its cohomology map is the composite of the isomorphism in step 5 and the map induced by a cochain isomorphism. The localization $Q$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Using its compatibility with shift gives precisely the claimed isomorphism $Q(\check B_E)\to Q(\check B_v)[1]$, represented by $Q(\check\theta\circ\check p)$.

lean.statement: theorem excision [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} ℚ)] (a : E) (hcard : 2 ≤ Fintype.card E) : (∃ (e : Deleted a) (f : Deleted a →o Deleted a), e.val.val = {a} ∧ (∀ S : Deleted a, (f S).val.val = insert a S.val.val) ∧ (∀ S : Deleted a, S ≤ f S ∧ e ≤ f S)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, IsZero ((complex ℚ (Deleted a)).homology n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Function.Injective ((inclusion a).f n)) ∧ ((inclusion a).f (-1) (bracket ℚ (-1) ([] : List (Deleted a))) = bracket ℚ (-1) ([] : List (Proper (Finset.univ : Finset E)))) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → IsZero ((quotientComplex a).X n) ∧ IsZero ((suspension (booleanComplex (coatom a))).X n)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℤ) (c : Simplex (Proper (Finset.univ : Finset E)) n), (theta a hcard).hom.f n ((projection a).f n (Finsupp.single c 1)) = signedDeletion a n (Finsupp.single c 1)) ∧ IsIso (derivedComparison a hcard)
